name: mcs-08-rna-protein-composition
title: Composition scale — the RNA/protein growth law

cites.claim: RNA/protein mass ratio increases with growth rate in E. coli
ribosomal fraction rises linearly with growth rate (C-line)

question: Does v2ecoli reproduce the Bremer-Dennis growth law that the RNA/protein mass ratio rises with growth rate — a completely different observable (bulk chemical composition) from the signaling/metabolism/heterogeneity arcs — and is the slope consistent with the measured law?
hypothesis: RNA/protein rises with growth rate (more ribosomes at faster growth). v2ecoli reproduces the positive slope natively; the magnitude discriminates whether ribosome/rRNA allocation is correctly growth-coupled.
objective: Read RNA and protein mass from native mass listeners at two growth rates (minimal glucose, amino-acid-rich), compute RNA/protein vs growth rate, and compare the slope direction to the Bremer-Dennis law.
readouts: RNA/protein mass ratio (listeners.mass.rna_mass / protein_mass) per condition

expected_behavior.name: rna-protein-rises-with-growth
expected_behavior.rationale: Bremer-Dennis: RNA/protein rises with growth rate (ribosome content increases).

tests.name: rna-protein-rises-with-growth
tests.question: Does RNA/protein increase from minimal to rich medium?

measure.detail: slope of rna_mass/protein_mass vs growth_rate across conditions; positive expected.

visualizations.name: Emergent growth laws (triptych)
visualizations.description: Three independent bacterial growth laws — Cooper-Helmstetter, Scott-Hwa, Bremer-Dennis — reproduced natively (direction), literature overlaid.

rna-protein-rises-with-growth.detail: RNA/protein 0.310 (mu 0.90/h) -> 0.318 (mu 1.28/h); slope +0.021 per (1/h), POSITIVE, reproducing the Bremer-Dennis direction. Magnitude shallow (~3% rise) across the amino-acid axis (R-line); the carbon-quality (C-line) ladder is covered by mcs-07.

claim: v2ecoli reproduces the Bremer-Dennis composition law DIRECTION natively: RNA/protein mass ratio rises with growth rate (0.310->0.318, slope +0.021/h). The rise is shallow across the amino-acid (R-line) axis, echoing the flat ribosome concentration seen in mcs-01/mcs-07 on that axis; the carbon-quality (C-line) ladder (mcs-07) is where the ribosomal fraction climbs steeply.

findings.statement: v2ecoli reproduces the qualitative Bremer-Dennis growth law: the RNA/protein mass ratio rises with growth rate, from 0.310 at mu 0.90/h (minimal glucose) to 0.318 at mu 1.28/h (amino-acid-rich), a positive slope of +0.021 per (1/h). The direction is correct and emerges from the native mass balance. The magnitude is shallow — only a ~3% rise in RNA/protein for a 43% rise in growth rate — where the classic law predicts a steeper climb. This is consistent with the two conditions spanning an amino-acid-supply (R-line) axis rather than a carbon-quality (C-line) series: supplying amino acids raises growth without demanding proportionally more ribosomes. The C-line test (where ribosomal fraction tracks growth steeply) is carried by the sibling study mcs-07, which shows ribosome concentration climbing across an acetate/succinate/glucose carbon ladder.

expected.summary: Bremer-Dennis / Scott 2010: RNA/protein (ribosome content) rises ~linearly with growth rate; the C-line slope is steep.

findings.next_action: The carbon-quality (C-line) ladder is covered by mcs-07; a denser composition ladder would quantify the slope.
caveats: Two conditions only (a first result); the amino-acid axis is the R-line, not the classic C-line.

biological_summary: One of microbiology's most robust laws: faster-growing cells commit more mass to ribosomes, so the RNA/protein mass ratio climbs with growth rate (Bremer-Dennis). v2ecoli reproduces the direction natively; the magnitude is shallow on the amino-acid (R-line) axis (the steep C-line is mcs-07's carbon ladder).

behavior_tests.name: rna-protein-rises-with-growth
behavior_tests.measure: slope of RNA/protein mass ratio vs growth rate
